lines.text: Two cameras send dozens of photos a second. Each one is a little off. Far away, by a couple of centimeters. Up close, by a couple of millimeters.
So the robot keeps one estimate and nudges it toward each new photo: a lot for close, sharp photos, and only a little for far, fuzzy ones.
A photo that jumps more than twenty five centimeters is ignored, unless three in a row agree. And unsure photos, where the tag could be facing two ways, are skipped.
Three photos that agree, and the robot is locked on.
In the last few centimeters the tag leaves the camera's view, so the robot finishes on its smooth wheel pose.
